items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Charlie Creff, you might have heard of him, and Dewey Jackson, you know. They were featured there.

ctx.x: You weren't a bad boy or anything? Oh no, no.

I'd never been to drugs, that's good. I'd never been to trouble. The only time I would have been in trouble, if you may recall, they put us all in jail in Memphis, the whole band. See we played, we did six weeks and when we left, see it was supposed to be a big dance here at the end of this game out there. And it's supposed to have some government warehouse or something like that. Anyhow, people came far away from Florida and Mississippi, you know, and Ramport Street and the people just, these little flippers,…

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Charlie Crep, yeah. He was great.

ctx.x: I talked to him the other day.

He had a studio right there at 36th Estate you know. He had the band in Milwaukee, the Wisconsin roof, before Sims had it. He comes or he leaves there and goes to Savoy. That's when Sims goes on in there and when Sims is about a year or so I go in there with Sims. But he had a good band, he had a good band, he had good Harmon's Bremen. He had Riverview. He and Cook, those fellas, they had some of the best jobs to be had. McGuire's down on Clark Street. I follow Roy and Dutray and him all around. And I get into…
Yeah, he's from Denver but he's been there.
